rounds.text: Corona Remedies Ltd is backed by elite operational performance, featuring a return on capital employed of 33.3% and a 3-year median return on equity of 27% [E12, E18]. This superior profitability far exceeds sector benchmarks, with ROE sitting at 24.79% against a sector median of 10.37% and ROCE at 27.13% versus 11.82% [E9, E10]. Growth metrics reinforce this quality, demonstrated by a 17% compounded sales growth over 3 years accelerating to 18% in the trailing twelve months, alongside 33% compounded profit growth over 3 years [E14, E15, E16]. Furthermore, institutional sponsorship is surging with positive money flow as foreign and domestic institutions increased their holdings by a combined 7.92 percentage points up to June 2026, while the rules-based screen awards the company a strong 86 out of 100 [E33, E34, E35, E52]. Conceded: the stock trades at an elevated valuation including a P/E of 60.8x and a price-to-book of 17.30x, alongside a discounted cash flow pointing to an intrinsic value of Rs 1326 [E1, E2, E36].

Corona Remedies Ltd trades at an extreme valuation that is wholly detached from its intrinsic value, with a price-to-earnings ratio of 60.8x and a price-to-book multiple of 17.30x that vastly exceed sector benchmarks of 33.34x and 3.15x respectively [E1, E2, E6, E7]. This excessive pricing leaves the stock severely overvalued, as demonstrated by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 1326 per share against a market price of Rs 2111, resulting in a staggering margin of safety of -59.2% [E36, E37]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF reveals that the current market price already bakes in an unrealistic 24.5% earnings growth rate, surpassing even the base case assumption of 18.0%, while explicit screen warnings flag that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E38, E57]. The company's balance sheet and operational quality also harbour notable cracks, evidenced by a current ratio of 0.96x indicating that current liabilities exceed current assets, a nearly doubled borrowing level of Rs 165 Cr compared to Rs 86 Cr a year prior, and a specific negative flag suggesting the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E29, E30, E51]. Technical indicators compound these fundamental warnings, with the stock trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E41]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong financial productivity through a high ROCE of 33.3% and a robust 3-year compounded profit growth of 33% [E12, E16].
